algorithm.title: Algorithmic Approach to Neonatal Jaundice (from AAP).

cell.label: Newborn infant
Assess for jaundice every 8-12 hours.
Is jaundice present?
Is age <24 hours or does jaundice by visual assessment or TcB appear severe enough to require TSB or TcB?
Measure TSB or TcB and interpret by age in hours.
Is TSB >95th percentile?
(1) Evaluate cause; (2) Treat if criteria for treatment is met; (3) Repeat TSB in 4-24 hours.
Evaluate TSB level, gestational age and hours of life. Treat if criteria for treatment is met.
Any repeat TSB drawn?
Is TSB level increasing across percentile line?
Has TcB or TSB been measured?
Is newborn ready for discharge?
Any risk factors or infant <72 hours old?
Follow up by 48-120 hours of age, exact timing depends upon age in hours and presence of risk factors. See .
Is follow-up assured?
Discharge with planned follow-up.*
Measure TSB or TcB if not already done, assure plan for follow-up and/or management* according to billirubin level.
Discharge and follow-up at physician discretion.*
Evaluate TSB level, gestational age and hours of life. Treat if criteria for treatment is met.
Evaluate cause, treat if criteria are met, and repeat TSB in 4-24 hours (as above).
Continue to assess for jaundice every 8-12 hours (above).

footnotes.footnote: *Provide information and written guidelines about jaundice to parents of all newborns at discharge.
From Management of hyperbilirubinemia in the newborn infant 35 or more weeks of gestation. Subcommittee on Hyperbilirubinemia. Pediatrics 2004;114:297-316.
